Q1: In a full-scan security audit, what should happen when a non-binary tracked text file is skipped because it is over the per-file cap (`over_file_cap`) or the total cap (`over_total_cap`)? Binary files are skipped as they are today in every option.
Choices:
A. Let the audit run and post its findings, but don't record the commit as audited (don't move the `<!-- ai:security-audit-last-sha:… -->` marker). Mark coverage as partial on the tracker and send a warning that names the skipped files, so the next run audits the full repository again. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Fail closed. Stop the audit before the model runs with an `oversized-scope` failure: no findings posted and no marker update. The weekly audit stays blocked until the file shrinks or an operator raises `SECURITY_AUDIT_OVERSIZED_FILE_MAX_BYTES` / `SECURITY_AUDIT_OVERSIZED_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES`.
C. Inspect over-cap text files in 1 MiB chunks anyway. In full-scan mode, drop the per-file cap and keep only the hard 256 MiB include limit (`MAX_INCLUDE_TOTAL`). Whatever still doesn't fit is handled as in A.
A+C. Do both: chunk as much as possible (C), and never record the commit as audited while any text file is left uninspected (A).
